newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -July 24.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -July 24.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST

News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Public Relations, Sponsoring, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING, PUBLIC RELATIONS & SPONSORING:

FRANKFURT - The German federal finance ministry has backed a plan to allow sponsors to write off their expenditures as business expenses when the sponsorship is intended to improve the company's public image. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung) *********
DUESSELDORF - Local Benetton retailers cannot hold the Italian company's controversial ad campaign responsible for losses in turnover, the federal court in Karlsruhe decides. (Handelsblatt) *********

FRANKFURT - Peter Rogge dissolves the strategic alliance between his Rogge & Partner agency and the Publicis Network and plans to work independently again at a new company: Peter Rogge Creative Consulting in Frankfurt. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Ad agency Buehler & Partner (B&P) says it has won the European-wide account for radiator brand Stelrad. The British manufacturer Caradon Plc wants B&P to design its European communications strategy. (Reuter)
MUNICH - British airline Britannia Airways Ltd awards its press and public relations account for its German unit to the Munich-based PR agency Wilde & Partner, the agency says. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
FRANKFURT - The 50 largest German publishing houses boosted turnover by nearly eight percent last year fuelled by strong growth among the top three companies, trade magazine Horizont says. (Reuter)

LUDWIGSHAFEN - The association of state media authorities calls for the agreement over digital television between CLT-Ufa, the Kirch group and Deutsche Telekom to be made public. The authorities say the information is particularly important for private cable companies and programming providers. (Reuter) *********
KISSING - Trade publishing group Weka says it has entered the Spanish market by buying a 20-percent share of publishing house Civitas. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
MUNICH - Bayerische Vereinsbank AG says it expects to post a good profit this year after its operating profit rose by a slightly below forecast 15.2 percent in the first half. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Commerzbank AG reports a bigger-than-expected 23.2-percent rise in operating profit and tries to quash talk that the bank faces takeover or merger, saying its earnings show it can stay independent. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG says its passenger numbers rose 5.7 percent to 20.8 million in the first half of 1997 from 19.682 million a year earlier. (Reuter)
ESSEN - German department store group Karstadt says it is on course to nearly treble net profits this year after earnings slid in 1996 and forced management to cut the dividend.
(Reuter)

FRANKFURT - SAP AG, a fast-growing German software house, says it hopes to exceed its 1997 sales growth targets, and says first half sales and profits were boosted by the weaker deutschemark. (Reuter)

BONN - Germans bought more beverages last year than in 1995, says the association of refreshments manufacturers (BDE). The industry group says turnover grew by 2.9 percent last year and production increased by 2.1 percent. The BDE says 1997 looks to be less successful. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Trade fair company Messe Frankfurt GmbH says it is interested in forming partnerships with other congress centre businesses. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
STUTTGART - Hans-Bernhard Port, the German sales director of sports car manufacturer Porsche AG, moves to U.S. giant Chrysler. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Stefano Caroti is named new general manager for central Europe at sportswear maker Nike. Caroti was previously general manager of Nike Italy. (Horizont)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
